page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors built on 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, managed via the Nitro hypervisor. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, along with hardware AES acceleration. The system delivers 128 GB of RAM, producing a high 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core. It includes a 475 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. No GPUs are provisioned.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced memory bandwidth alongside moderate multi-core compute capability. The instance records an average stress-ng multi-core score of 12111.79 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5442.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 122.36 GB/sec, while write bandwidth sustains 57.08 GB/sec. Single-threaded metrics are lower, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 970.0 and lower scores in compression tests like gzip and bzip3. However, memory-focused operations show steady throughput, yielding 9.33 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 5248.33.

From an architectural standpoint, the ARM-based Graviton design provides high memory density with lower qualitative power and operational overhead relative to x86 alternatives. A primary hardware tradeoff is lower per-core compute output and instruction set limits compared to compute-optimized platforms. Given its 128 GB memory footprint and fast local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis or Memcached clusters, real-time data ingestion, and memory-bound caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.2xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with dedicated physical cores, it couples 128 GB of system memory with a 475 GB local NVMe SSD. The configuration delivers an expansive 16:1 memory-to-core ratio alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate steady multi-core scaling, reaching 12111.79 in stress-ng multi-core and 9.33 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core compute metrics remain in lower percentiles. The combination of high memory capacity, dedicated NVMe temporary storage, and energy-efficient ARM silicon offers dense resource allocation for memory-heavy environments. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large caching layers, key-value stores, and database workloads requiring high RAM per core.
